title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two past weeks at $4.56: 195 (-7%) and 119 (-43%); average 22% below baseline. Shrink toward 1.0 due to noise and few data points. Adjust down 12% for price sensitivity.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (new driver)
drivers.evidence: No prior occurrence; only speculative. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0. Low confidence. Suggests modest uplift, but not reliable.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. No events are scheduled, but the price is raised 5.1% above regular ($4.56 vs $4.34). Past price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show demand dropped to 195 and 119 units—22% and 43% below baseline—suggesting sensitivity. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical precedent; noise-adjusted effect is uncertain. No past promotion at this price level. The classical model’s 1.00 multiplier is too neutral. We adjust down for price increase, with low confidence in TikTok lift. No evidence of seasonal ramp or trend change.

brief:

TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.3 - 290.5 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
